name: Digital Europe Programme
evidence_rating: thin: Commission interim evaluation reports outputs and user ratings; no counterfactual or independent study of impact found
summary: Digital Europe (EUR 8.2bn, 2021-2027) funds supercomputers, AI and cybersecurity infrastructure, innovation hubs and advanced skills. The Commission's 2025 mid-term review shows outputs largely on track - the JUPITER exascale computer, over 150 innovation hubs serving 54,600 firms and 20,700 people trained - but effects on firms' productivity or digital uptake have not been measured, and no independent evaluation was found.

indicators.objective: The proposal's financial statement contains no usable LFS indicators (1.4.4 in the extraction covers synergies); performance indicators per specific objective are set in Annex II of the Regulation, and the IA said indicators would also draw on the Digital Economy and Society Index

indicators.indicator: Joint procurements of HPC infrastructure; use of exascale systems
indicators.evidence: 19 of 30 planned procurements done; JUPITER, the EU's first exascale computer, ranked 4th on TOP500 and 1st on Green500 (its JEDI module); 19 AI Factories being deployed.

indicators.indicator: Number of European Digital Innovation Hubs and businesses served
indicators.evidence: Over 150 EDIHs covering 90% of regions by end-2024; 29,000 services to 54,600 companies; users value services at EUR 8,000-15,300 per organisation (perceived value, not measured effect).

indicators.indicator: People trained; master's programmes and courses
indicators.evidence: By end-2024: 50+ master's programmes, 530 short courses, 20,700+ people trained in AI, cybersecurity, semiconductors etc.
26 CyberHubs procured (in line with targets); network of 27 national coordination centres; first 12 cybersecurity tools deployed.

indicators.indicator: Higher EU digital capacity and uptake (e.g. SMEs highly digitised 20% in 2018)
indicators.evidence: Interim evaluation: programme on track or ahead on activities and outputs, first outcome-level benefits only now emerging; no measured effect on productivity, uptake or competitiveness.

literature.citation: European Commission (2018), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal establishing the Digital Europe programme (executive summary SWD(2018) 306), SWD(2018) 305
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal establishing the Digital Europe programme (executive summary SWD(2018) 306)
literature.outcomes: digital investment gap; HPC; AI; cybersecurity; skills
literature.headline: Identifies an upstream investment gap: EU consumes one third of world HPC resources but provides about 5%; HPC investment at 60% of US level; only 20% of SMEs highly digitised; no quantified impact forecast
literature.summary_plain: The Commission said Europe was under-investing in supercomputers, AI, cybersecurity and digital skills and proposed a dedicated deployment programme, without forecasting measurable economic gains.

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), Interim Evaluation of the Digital Europe Programme (Staff Working Document) and report COM(2025) 771, SWD(2025) 420; COM(2025) 771
literature.title: Interim Evaluation of the Digital Europe Programme (Staff Working Document) and report COM(2025) 771
literature.method: interim evaluation (monitoring data, surveys, perceived-value study)
literature.headline: Implementation initially delayed by late legal basis but accelerated; on track or ahead on outputs; JUPITER exascale system; 150+ EDIHs serving 54,600 companies; 20,700 people trained; 26 CyberHubs; administrative costs 4.9%; outcome-level benefits only emerging
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's mid-term review finds the EUR 8.2bn programme has delivered its planned supercomputers, innovation hubs and training places, but evidence on effects for firms or the economy is still limited to user ratings.
literature.verified: full text read (report; SWD key sections)
